mainTopic: A betrothed נערה who grew up before her trial, where she and an idol worshipper are stoned, and the penalties of the מוציא שם רע
overview: The גמרא first rejects the attempt to tie שילא's ruling (that a betrothed נערה who sinned and then became a בוגרת gets חנק) to רבי שמעון's view about a כהן גדול or נשיא who sinned before being appointed. It then brings רבי יוחנן, who rules she gets סקילה, and רבי אילעא, who learns this from the word ״הנערה״, meaning the girl she was when she sinned. רבי חנניא objects: then her false accuser should also get מלקות and pay מאה סלע. The גמרא answers that her punishment follows her act, done as a נערה, while his follows his speech, said when she was already a בוגרת. A ברייתא then teaches where a נערה המאורסה and an idol worshipper are stoned: at her father's doorway or the city gate, at the gate where he worshipped, and at the בית דין in a city that is mostly גוים. These rules are learned from the word ״שעריך״ and from רבי אבהו's chain פתח, פתח, שער, שעריך. Finally, a ברייתא about the מוציא שם רע is explained in two ways. רבי יהודה's 'flogged in any case' is shown to mean rabbinic מכת מרדות.

steps.title: רבי שמעון may only add awareness, not replace the time of the sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof that שילא follows רבי שמעון. רבי שמעון counts the time of ידיעה as well as the time of חטאה, but he never said ידיעה alone decides.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, we know רבי שמעון also looks at the time of awareness. But did you ever hear him say he looks only at the awareness and ignores the time of the sin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pushing back on the earlier idea that שילא's ruling (חנק for a girl who grew up before her trial) matches רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said a כהן גדול or נשיא who sinned before being appointed, and found out only after, is exempt. He cannot bring a commoner's offering, because the awareness came after his rank changed. That shows he counts ידיעה in addition to חטאה. It does not show that ידיעה alone decides, which is what שילא's ruling would need.

keyTerms.meaning: Awareness, the moment the sinner finds out he sinned
The sin itself, the time it was done

steps.confusionAlert: 'אף בתר ידיעה' (even after awareness) is not the same as 'only after awareness'. רבי שמעון needs BOTH times. He does not let awareness replace the time of the sin.

phrases.english: Say that we heard regarding Rabbi Shimon
that he follows even the time of awareness;
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון also takes into account when the כהן גדול or king found out about his sin.

phrases.english: that he follows the awareness

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אָזֵיל בָּתַר חֶטְאָה מִי שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: and does not follow the sin, did you hear him say that?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימוֹר דְּשָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the earlier claim that שילא's ruling follows רבי שמעון
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רבי שמעון for שילא's ruling
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof treats 'awareness also matters' as if it meant 'only awareness matters'

steps.title: Proof: otherwise he would bring the offering of his new rank
steps.stepSummary: If רבי שמעון went only by the time of awareness, the newly appointed כהן גדול would bring a פר and the נשיא a שעיר. Since he doesn't say that, he must also care about the time of the sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let him bring the offering that fits his status now: the anointed כהן גדול brings a bull, and the king brings a goat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its rejection with a proof. If awareness alone decided, רבי שמעון's ruling would come out differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול brings a פר and a נשיא brings a שעיר for their sins. רבי שמעון does not require these special offerings. He exempts the person entirely. That shows the time of the sin (when he was a commoner) still counts, so the comparison to שילא falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The anointed one, the כהן גדול

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן — לַיְיתֵי קׇרְבָּן כִּי דְּהַשְׁתָּא:
phrases.english: If so, let him bring an offering fitting his current status:
the anointed one a bull, and the king a goat!

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון needs both the sin and the awareness to happen in the same status. So he is no source for judging the girl only by her status at the trial.
steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן לַיְיתֵי קׇרְבָּן כִּי דְּהַשְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in step 1 with a logical proof
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון does not follow only the time of awareness
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון does not require a פר or שעיר from someone who sinned before his appointment

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: teach that she is stoned
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן told the תנא who recited שילא's ruling to change it: the girl gets סקילה, not חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't רבי יוחנן say to the תנא: Teach that she is judged with stoning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן, who disagrees with שילא and rules that she gets סקילה. This sets up the next question: why?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the link to רבי שמעון was rejected, there is still a real debate here. רבי יוחנן holds that the girl is judged by her status when she sinned, so she gets the נערה המאורסה punishment of סקילה.

keyTerms.meaning: A scholar who memorized and recited teachings of the תנאים

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say to the tanna:
phrases.notes: This is the תנא who had just recited שילא's ruling that she gets חנק.

phrases.english: Teach: she is judged with stoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְתַנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the issue is still debated, after the רבי שמעון comparison was rejected
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A betrothed נערה who sinned and then became a בוגרת is judged with סקילה

steps.title: But the verse speaks of a young girl, and she is now grown
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. The Torah gives סקילה to a נערה המאורסה, but this girl is now a בוגרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? The Torah said 'a betrothed young girl', and this one is a grown woman!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's ruling using the wording of the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סקילה is only for a נערה המאורסה. By the time of her trial she is a בוגרת, so she seems to fall outside that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothed young girl (roughly ages 12 to 12½)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
A grown woman, past the age of נערה

phrases.english: But why?
The Merciful One said 'a betrothed young girl'
but this one is a grown woman!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse requires a נערה, and she is now a בוגרת

steps.title: רבי אילעא: 'the girl' she already was
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא answers that the word ״הנערה״ (THE girl) means the girl she was when she sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said: The verse says 'the girl', meaning the girl she already was.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעא defends רבי יוחנן with a reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'the' points back to the girl as she was at the time of the sin. So her status at that moment decides her punishment, even though she has since grown up.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a said: The verse states:
'The girl', the girl that she already was.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that her punishment follows her status at the time of the act. The rest of the סוגיא builds on it.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'נערה' means her status now, at the trial
steps.terutzMaskana: 'הנערה' means her status when she sinned

steps.title: Then the husband should also get lashes and pay 100 סלע
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנניא argues that if she counts as a נערה, then a husband who falsely accuses her should also get מלקות and pay מאה סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנניא said to רבי אילעא: If so, let him also get lashes, and let him also pay the hundred sela!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנניא challenges רבי אילעא by applying his rule to the husband who falsely accuses her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah punishes a husband who falsely accuses his נערה wife (מוציא שם רע) with מלקות and a fine of מאה סלע. If she still counts as a נערה, those penalties should apply to him too, even though she is now a בוגרת.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine of one hundred sela coins

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא לְרַבִּי אִילְעָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chananya said to Rabbi Ile'a:
If so, let him also be lashed,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the husband who falsely claimed she sinned while betrothed.

phrases.english: and let him also pay the hundred sela!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי מִילְקָא נָמֵי לִילְקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אילעא's answer by pushing its logic further
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אילעא's rule that her status at the time of the sin decides
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being consistent would require the husband's penalties too, yet those are not given

steps.title: רבי אילעא: Heaven save us from that view
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא sharply rejects רבי חנניא's argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: May the Merciful One save us from this opinion!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעא pushes away רבי חנניא's challenge without explaining why yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He treats the comparison as plainly wrong: the husband's penalty should not follow her status at the time of her sin. The real reason comes later, in steps 10 and 11.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַחֲמָנָא נַיצְּלַן מֵהַאי דַּעְתָּא:
phrases.english: He said to him: May the Merciful One save us from this opinion!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַחֲמָנָא נַיצְּלַן מֵהַאי דַּעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי חנניא's challenge
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between her punishment and the husband's
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not stated here; it is explained in steps 10 and 11

steps.title: רבי חנניא: on the contrary, save us from yours
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנניא answers back that it is רבי אילעא's view that needs saving from.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, may the Merciful One save us from your opinion!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנניא turns the phrase around and rejects רבי אילעא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each one thinks the other's view is clearly wrong. This leaves an open question about why her punishment and his could follow different times, and the next step asks it.

phrases.english: On the contrary, may the Merciful One save us from your opinion!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה רַחֲמָנָא נַיצְּלַן מִדַּעְתָּא דִּידָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers back to רבי אילעא's rejection
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי חנניא sees the different treatment of her and the husband as baseless

steps.title: What is the reason for the difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why she is treated as a נערה for her punishment, but as a בוגרת when it comes to the husband's penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the logic behind רבי אילעא's view. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is how one girl can count as a נערה for one law and a בוגרת for another.

phrases.english: And what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטַעְמָא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבי אילעא's rejection
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why her punishment and the husband's penalty follow different times

steps.title: Her deeds caused hers, his lips caused his
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר אבין (or רבי יצחק בר אבא) explains that she is punished for her act, while he is punished for his words.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one, her actions caused her punishment; and that one, the twisting of his lips caused his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer in a short, catchy form.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her punishment is tied to an act. His penalty is tied to speech, the false claim (עקימת שפתיו). Since the two sins happen at different times, each one can follow its own moment.

keyTerms.meaning: The twisting of his lips, meaning sinning through speech

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אָבִין, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Avin said, and some say Rabbi Yitzchak bar Abba:
This one, her actions caused her punishment,
and that one, the twisting of his lips caused his.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the husband, whose sin was the false accusation he spoke.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ מַעֲשֶׂיהָ גָּרְמוּ לָהּ וְזֶה עֲקִימַת שְׂפָתָיו גָּרְמוּ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Her punishment follows her act; his follows his speech

steps.title: She sinned as a girl; he spoke when she was grown
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the phrases and explains them. She sinned while a נערה, so she gets סקילה. He spoke when she was already a בוגרת, so he gets no מלקות and pays no מאה סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Her actions caused her punishment: when she sinned, she sinned as a girl. His lips caused his: when does he become liable? At the time he speaks, and at that time she was a grown woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the short answer of step 10 and applies it to each person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each punishment follows the moment its own sin happened. For her, that moment is the act, when she was a נערה. For him, it is the accusation, when she was already a בוגרת. So there is no contradiction, and רבי חנניא's challenge is answered.

phrases.english: This one, her actions caused her punishment:
when she committed adultery, she committed it as a young girl.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording.

phrases.english: And that one, the twisting of his lips caused his:
when does he become liable?

phrases.aramaic: הָהִיא שַׁעְתָּא, וְהָהִיא שַׁעְתָּא בּוֹגֶרֶת הֲוַאי.
phrases.english: At that time, and at that time she was a grown woman.

steps.whatToRemember: Each punishment follows the time of its own sin. She sinned by her act while a נערה, so she gets סקילה. He sinned by speaking once she was a בוגרת, so he gets no מלקות and pays no מאה סלע.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a contradiction about her status. The question is not 'what is she?' but 'when did each person's sin happen?'
steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ מַעֲשֶׂיהָ גָּרְמוּ לָהּ כִּי זַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the words of step 10 in order to explain and apply them
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Her punishment follows her status when she acted (נערה, so סקילה). The husband's penalty follows the time he spoke (בוגרת, so no מלקות or מאה סלע).

steps.title: Where a betrothed young woman who committed adultery is stoned
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three possible places to stone a נערה המאורסה who committed adultery: her father's doorway, the city gate, or the doorway of the בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: a betrothed young woman who committed adultery is stoned at the entrance of her father's house. If she has no father's house, she is stoned at the gate of that city. In a city that is mostly gentiles, she is stoned at the entrance of the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא that tells us exactly where a נערה המאורסה is stoned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first choice is her father's doorway. If that is not possible, the city gate is used. If the city is mostly גוים, the stoning moves to the doorway of the בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: A young woman (between 12 and 12½) who is betrothed but not yet fully married
They stone (carry out the death penalty of סקילה)
The entrance of her father's house
A city whose population is mostly gentiles

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A betrothed young woman who committed adultery:

phrases.aramaic: סוֹקְלִין אוֹתָהּ עַל פֶּתַח בֵּית אָבִיהָ.
phrases.english: one stones her at the entrance of her father's house.
If she has no entrance of a father's house,

phrases.aramaic: סוֹקְלִין אוֹתָהּ עַל פֶּתַח שַׁעַר הָעִיר הַהִיא.
phrases.english: one stones her at the entrance of the gate of that city.
And in a city that is mostly gentiles,

phrases.aramaic: סוֹקְלִין אוֹתָהּ עַל פֶּתַח בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: one stones her at the entrance of the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נַעֲרָה הַמְאוֹרָסָה שֶׁזִּינְּתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about the place of execution, moving on from the discussion of the husband's penalty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נערה המאורסה who committed adultery is stoned at her father's doorway. If there is none, she is stoned at the city gate. In a city that is mostly גוים, she is stoned at the doorway of the בית דין.

steps.title: The same pattern for someone who worshipped idols
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds a similar rule: an idol worshipper is stoned at the gate where he worshipped, or at the בית דין if the city is mostly גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a similar way you say: one who worshipped idols is stoned at the gate where he worshipped. In a city that is mostly gentiles, he is stoned at the entrance of the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא gives a parallel case: where a person who worshipped עבודה זרה is stoned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the main place is tied to where the sin happened, the gate where he worshipped. The backup in a city of mostly גוים is the same as before: the doorway of the בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: In a similar way; a parallel case

phrases.english: In a similar way you say:
One who worshipped idols:

phrases.aramaic: סוֹקְלִין אוֹתוֹ עַל שַׁעַר שֶׁעָבַד בּוֹ,
phrases.english: one stones him at the gate where he worshipped,
and in a city that is mostly gentiles,

phrases.aramaic: סוֹקְלִין אוֹתוֹ עַל פֶּתַח בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: one stones him at the entrance of the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּיּוֹצֵא בַּדָּבָר אַתָּה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a parallel case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An idol worshipper is stoned at the gate where he worshipped. In a city that is mostly גוים, he is stoned at the doorway of the בית דין.

steps.title: What is the source for this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that the idol worshipper is stoned at the gate where he worshipped.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule about the idol worshipper. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the idol worshipper is stoned at the gate where he worshipped, and the גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this. The source for the נערה's city-gate rule is asked separately in step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these things learned? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters learned?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the idol worshipper rule from Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the תורה for stoning an idol worshipper at the gate where he worshipped.

steps.title: The word "your gates" means the gate where he worshipped
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא answers that the פסוק's word ״שעריך״ means the gate where he worshipped.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Sages taught: "Your gates" means the gate where he worshipped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The word ״שעריך״ in the פסוק about stoning an idol worshipper refers to the gate where he worshipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says to bring him out "to your gates" and stone him. The ברייתא reads this as the gate of the city where the sin happened.

keyTerms.meaning: "Your gates", the key word in the פסוק

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
"Your gates": this is the gate where he worshipped.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁעָרֶיךָ זֶה שַׁעַר שֶׁעָבַד בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source in Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ״שעריך״ in דברים 17:5 refers to the gate where he worshipped.

steps.title: Maybe it means the gate where he was judged?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether ״שעריך״ might instead mean the gate where the בית דין sentenced him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it is the gate where he worshipped? Or perhaps it is only the gate where he was judged?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own reading. Maybe "your gates" means the court's gate, not the place of the sin. This sets up the proof that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In those times courts sat at the city gates, so "gate" could easily mean the place of judgment. The ברייתא needs a proof to rule this other reading out.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it is only... (introduces another possible reading)
The gate where he was judged (the court's location)

phrases.english: Do you say it is the gate where he worshipped,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא שַׁעַר שֶׁנִּידּוֹן בּוֹ?
phrases.english: or is it only the gate where he was judged?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר שַׁעַר שֶׁעָבַד בּוֹ אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא שַׁעַר שֶׁנִּידּוֹן בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reading given in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether ״שעריך״ means the gate where he worshipped or the gate where he was sentenced.

steps.title: Proof from the earlier "your gates" in the same section
steps.stepSummary: A גזירה שוה: ״שעריך״ is used both earlier and later in the section. Just as the earlier one means the place of worship, so does the later one.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Your gates" is said below, and "your gates" is said above. Just as "your gates" stated above is the gate where he worshipped, so too "your gates" stated below is the gate where he worshipped.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves its first reading. It compares the word ״שעריך״ in the stoning פסוק to the same word a few פסוקים earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier פסוק (17:2) describes the sin taking place "in one of your gates", so there it clearly means where he worshipped. Because the same word appears in both places, the later use takes the same meaning. That rules out "the gate where he was judged".

keyTerms.meaning: Just as... so too... (the form of a comparison)

phrases.english: "Your gates" is stated below,
and "your gates" is stated above.
phrases.notes: דברים 17:2, where the sin is described.

phrases.english: Just as "your gates" stated above
is the gate where he worshipped,
so too "your gates" stated below
is the gate where he worshipped.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֱמַר שְׁעָרֶיךָ לְמַטָּה וְנֶאֱמַר שְׁעָרֶיךָ לְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16 and confirms the reading of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from ״שעריך״ in 17:2 shows that ״שעריך״ in 17:5 means the gate where he worshipped.
steps.whatToRemember: The idol worshipper is stoned where he sinned. We learn this by matching the word ״שעריך״ in the stoning פסוק to the same word in the פסוק that describes his sin.

steps.title: Another teaching: your gates, not gentile gates
steps.stepSummary: A second reading of ״שעריך״: it means Jewish gates, not the gates of a city of גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: "Your gates", and not the gates of gentiles.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא offers a different lesson from ״שעריך״: the stoning is done at Jewish city gates, not at the gates of a city of גוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the source for the rule in Steps 12–13: in a city that is mostly גוים, the stoning moves to the בית דין. The word "your" is read as "belonging to Jews".

keyTerms.meaning: Gates of gentiles (a city of mostly non-Jews)

phrases.english: Another explanation: "your gates", and not the gates of gentiles.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: שְׁעָרֶיךָ וְלֹא שַׁעֲרֵי גוֹיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a second, different lesson from the same word ״שעריך״.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״שעריך″ excludes the gates of a city of גוים, so there the stoning is done at the בית דין.

steps.title: But we already used that word
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: ״שעריך״ was already used to teach "the gate where he worshipped". How can it teach a second lesson?
steps.simpleTranslation: This "your gates": you already used it up!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second teaching. The same word cannot normally be used to teach two separate rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 already used ״שעריך״ for the גזירה שוה about the place of worship. Using it again for "not gentile gates" seems to count the word twice.

keyTerms.meaning: You already used it (for another teaching)

phrases.english: This "your gates": you already used it!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי שְׁעָרֶיךָ הָא אַפֵּיקְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 18 because the word was already used in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second teaching from ״שעריך״ in Step 18.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One word was already used for the first teaching, so it should not be available for a second one.

steps.title: The verse could have just said "gate"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: if only one lesson were meant, the verse would say ״שער״. The extra form ״שעריך״ shows a second lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the verse say "gate". Why does it say "your gates"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the second teaching. The verse chose a longer word than it needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the גזירה שוה alone, a plain ״שער״ would have been enough. The added "your" is extra, so it teaches a second rule: Jewish gates, not those of גוים.

keyTerms.meaning: What? Why? (here: why use this word?)

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say "gate";
why does it say "your gates"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן לֵימָא קְרָא שַׁעַר מַאי שְׁעָרֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording in the פסוק allows a second lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word ״שעריך״ is used up by the first teaching, so it cannot teach about gentile cities.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse needed only ״שער״. The fuller form ״שעריך״ is extra and teaches "not gentile gates".

steps.title: Two lessons from one word
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that ״שעריך״ teaches two things.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up: both lessons come from ״שעריך״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word teaches (1) the stoning is at the gate where he worshipped, and (2) not at the gates of a city of גוים, where it moves to the בית דין.

phrases.english: Learn two things from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ תַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the result of Step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ״שעריך״ teaches both that the idol worshipper is stoned at the gate where he worshipped, and that this does not apply to a city of mostly גוים, where he is stoned at the בית דין.
steps.whatToRemember: One word, two lessons: ״שעריך״ means the place of the sin (through the גזירה שוה), and the extra "your" means Jewish gates only.

steps.title: What is the source for a betrothed young woman?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא has a source for עבודה זרה being punished at the gate. Now it asks for the source for a נערה המאורסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for idol worship. From where do we know the same for a betrothed young woman?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts what it just learned about עבודה זרה. Now it asks where we learn the same gate rule for a נערה המאורסה. This question sets up רבי אבהו's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, ״שעריך״ taught that the idol worshipper is stoned at a gate. That פסוק talks only about עבודה זרה. So the גמרא needs a separate source to bring the city-gate rule over to a נערה המאורסה.

keyTerms.meaning: We found (a source for this case)
A betrothed young woman (after אירוסין, before נישואין)

phrases.english: We found [a source for] idol worship,
phrases.notes: This means the gate rule we just learned from ״שעריך״.

phrases.english: a betrothed young woman, from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, נַעֲרָה הַמְאוֹרָסָה מְנָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It builds on the conclusion about ״שעריך״ and asks how that rule extends to a new case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק source showing that a נערה המאורסה is stoned at the city gate, like an idol worshipper.

steps.title: A chain of words: entrance, entrance, gate, your gates
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו links the נערה המאורסה to עבודה זרה through a chain of matching words.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: we learn "entrance" from "entrance", "entrance" from "gate", and "gate" from "your gates".
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question. He builds a chain of matching words that carries the gate rule from עבודה זרה over to the נערה המאורסה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the נערה uses the word ״פתח״ (entrance). The משכן also has a ״פתח״, in the phrase "the entrance of the gate of the courtyard", so ״פתח״ there is tied to ״שער״. That ״שער״ is then linked to ״שעריך״ in the עבודה זרה פסוק, so the נערה is also punished at the gate.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns or derives (one word from another)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not one comparison. It is a three-link chain. Each link connects two places where a word appears, until we reach ״שעריך״.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
One learns "entrance" from "entrance",
phrases.notes: The first "entrance" is in דברים 22:21 about the נערה; the second is in במדבר 4:26, "the entrance of the gate of the courtyard".

phrases.english: and "entrance" from "gate",
phrases.notes: These two words sit right next to each other in that same משכן פסוק.

phrases.english: and "gate" from "your gates".

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: גָּמַר ״פֶּתַח״ מִ״פֶּתַח״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It directly answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A chained word-comparison: פתח to פתח to שער to שעריך. This carries the gate rule from עבודה זרה to the נערה המאורסה.
steps.whatToRemember: The city-gate rule for a נערה המאורסה comes from עבודה זרה through the chain פתח, פתח, שער, שעריך.

steps.title: A ברייתא on the punishment of a false accuser
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a dispute about whether a מוציא שם רע always pays one hundred סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: one who spreads a bad name is lashed and pays one hundred סלע. רבי יהודה says: he is always lashed, but he pays the hundred סלע only if he had relations with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about the husband who falsely accuses his wife (מוציא שם רע). It records two opinions about his punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that he gets מלקות. They disagree about the one hundred סלע fine. The תנא קמא makes no distinction, while רבי יהודה requires the payment only if the husband had relations with her.

keyTerms.meaning: One who falsely accuses his wife of unfaithfulness

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who brings out a bad name
phrases.notes: This is a husband who falsely claims his new wife was unfaithful while she was betrothed.

phrases.english: is lashed and gives one hundred sela.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
As for lashing, he is lashed in any case;
as for the one hundred sela:
if he had relations [with her], he gives;
if he did not have relations, he does not give.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמּוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע לוֹקֶה וְנוֹתֵן מֵאָה סֶלַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section. It moves from where the נערה is stoned to the punishment of the false accuser.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: מלקות plus one hundred סלע. רבי יהודה: מלקות always, but the one hundred סלע only if he had relations with her.

steps.title: Linking the ברייתא to the dispute of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the תנא קמא follows the רבנן and רבי יהודה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are arguing about the same thing as רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and the רבנן. The ברייתא means this: the מוציא שם רע is lashed and pays one hundred סלע whether or not he had relations, like the רבנן. רבי יהודה says he is always lashed, but pays only if he had relations, like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the ברייתא. It shows that its two opinions match a known dispute between רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא reads the ברייתא again and adds a few words to each side. The תנא קמא's words now say "whether he had relations or not", like the רבנן. רבי יהודה's view, paying only if he had relations, matches רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who ties the fine of the false accuser to a husband who had relations with his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what it means to say
Whether he had relations or did not

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree he gets מלקות. The only argument is about the one hundred סלע.
steps.whatToRemember: תנא קמא follows the רבנן: he pays either way. רבי יהודה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: he pays only if he had relations with her.

phrases.english: They are disagreeing about the dispute
of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov and the Rabbis.
And this is what it is saying:
One who brings out a bad name
is lashed and gives one hundred sela,
whether he had relations or did not have relations,
like the Rabbis.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
As for lashing, he is lashed in any case;
as for the one hundred sela:
if he had relations, he gives;
if he did not have relations, he does not give,
like Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא מִיפַּלְגִי בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It explains the ברייתא of step 24 by linking each opinion to a known earlier dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute in the ברייתא matches the dispute of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and the רבנן. The תנא קמא follows the רבנן, and רבי יהודה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.title: A second reading: the whole ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: Some say the entire ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. Both sides agree the 100 סלע needs prior relations, and רבי יהודה adds that flogging applies in any case.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are those who say: the whole ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and this is what it means: One who defames his wife is flogged and pays one hundred סלע, but only if he had relations with her. רבי יהודה says: as for flogging, he is flogged in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different explanation of the ברייתא from the one in step 25. Now both opinions follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and they argue only about flogging.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 25, the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה followed two different views. Here both accept רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's rule that the 100 סלע applies only if he had relations with her. The only argument left is whether the flogging also needs that condition. רבי יהודה says it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it: the entire ברייתא
Only if he had relations with her
In any case, no matter what

steps.confusionAlert: In this version רבי יהודה does NOT disagree about the 100 סלע. He agrees that the money needs prior relations. He argues only that the flogging does not need it.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
All of it follows Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.
And this is what it is saying:
One who spreads a bad name is flogged
and pays one hundred sela,
but only if he had relations with her.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
As for flogging, he is flogged in any case.
phrases.notes: He means: even if he never had relations with her, he still gets lashes. Only the money depends on that.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: כּוּלַּהּ כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation of the ברייתא instead of step 25's split between the רבנן and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees the 100 סלע needs prior relations. רבי יהודה holds that flogging applies even without them.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says רבי יהודה exempts from flogging without relations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה can say he is flogged in any case, when another ברייתא quotes him saying that without relations he is not flogged.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה really hold that he is flogged in any case? But it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says: if he had relations, he is flogged. If he did not have relations, he is not flogged!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה's words 'flogged in any case', which appear in the ברייתא and in both explanations of it. It brings another ברייתא where רבי יהודה seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our ברייתא, רבי יהודה says flogging applies even without relations. The other ברייתא quotes him clearly: no relations means no flogging. So the two quotes of רבי יהודה seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: And does he really hold? This opens a challenge.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yehuda hold
that as for flogging, he is flogged in any case?
But it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If he had relations, he is flogged;
if he did not have relations, he is not flogged!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לִלְקוֹת לוֹקֶה מִכׇּל מָקוֹם? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's 'flogged in any case' from the ברייתא, which appears in both readings (steps 25 and 26).
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's statement 'לִלְקוֹת לוֹקֶה מִכׇּל מָקוֹם' in the ברייתא of step 24, which both readings keep.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction between sources. Another ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה saying there is no flogging without relations.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the flogging is rabbinic מכת מרדות
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that 'flogged in any case' means rabbinic lashes for rebelliousness. The other ברייתא is talking about Torah lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: he is flogged with lashes for rebelliousness, which come from the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק settles the contradiction. The two quotes of רבי יהודה are about two different kinds of lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he had no relations with her, there are no Torah lashes, as the other ברייתא says. But the רבנן still give him מכת מרדות, rabbinic lashes for his bad behavior. That is what 'flogged in any case' means, so רבי יהודה's two statements no longer contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Lashes for rebelliousness: a punishment given by the רבנן, not by the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's 'flogged in any case' means rabbinic מכת מרדות when there were no relations. According to him, Torah lashes still need prior relations.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
he is flogged with lashes for rebelliousness
by rabbinic law.
phrases.notes: So the other ברייתא's 'not flogged' means no Torah lashes. Our ברייתא means rabbinic lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לוֹקֶה מַכַּת מַרְדּוּת מִדְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the two sources talk about different kinds of flogging (rabbinic vs. Torah).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'flogged in any case' meant Torah lashes, which would contradict the other ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means rabbinic מכת מרדות. Torah lashes still need prior relations, as the other ברייתא says.
